name: Gong Bingyan
about: I am Gong Bingyan, a Master of Cyber Security student at Universiti Malaya. My career focus is application security. I am interested in how software handles requests, permissions and data, and how developers can check that a repair works.

My background includes computing study, API and database projects, and an IT support internship. I have worked with Go, Python and Java and have used Linux and Docker in project work. My public projects include a Spring Boot security lab, an OpenList configuration-review platform and an identity-security prototype.

These projects let me examine ownership checks, API permissions, findings and audit events in code. Alongside them, WQE7001 lab records document network isolation and Nmap service discovery. I am still developing my security skills. I want readers to see the implementation, its evidence and its limits, with enough detail to review the work. My next priority is stronger identity handling and repeatable security regression tests.
career: My target is a junior application security or security testing role. I want to work with developers to understand a weakness, agree on a repair and check the result. My computing background gives me a starting point, but I still need stronger evidence of practical AppSec skills.

My next steps are to strengthen Linux and networking foundations, improve identity handling in my web security lab, and extend its security regression tests. By February 2027, I aim to replace the lab's request-parameter user simulation with trusted session-based identity and publish fresh results for two allowed and denied access-control scenarios, with setup instructions and clear results.

I will seek feedback on whether the work is correct and reproducible. GitHub stars can show interest, but tests, useful reviews and a verified repair will be my main quality checks. This is a development plan, not a claim that I already have professional AppSec experience.
